result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to the roadway without any protective buffer or street trees. The lack of marked crosswalks and lane markings, combined with parked cars that may obstruct sightlines, creates a moderately high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalks
hazards.description: The sidewalks are narrow and lack a buffer zone, placing pedestrians in close proximity to moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street, particularly the left side.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks visible, which may lead to unpredictable pedestrian crossings.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly designate pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with row houses built directly to the sidewalk edge. The pedestrian environment consists of a basic concrete walkway with no buffer from parked or moving vehicles, and a garage entrance that creates a potential conflict point.

hazards.name: Blind Driveway/Garage Conflict
hazards.description: A roll-up garage door opens directly onto the sidewalk, creating a point where vehicles may emerge with limited visibility of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, the grey building with the metal shutter.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the narrow sidewalk and the travel/parking lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible sidewalk edge.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Installing street trees or large planters would provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restricting parking immediately adjacent to the garage entrance to improve sightlines between exiting drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pavement Repairs
interventions.description: Repairing cracks and uneven surfaces in the concrete sidewalk to prevent trip hazards.

result.summary: The street is a wide, unmarked two-way roadway with narrow sidewalks on both sides and parallel parking. There is a lack of designated pedestrian crossing infrastructure, and the wide pavement width may encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential and commercial context.

hazards.name: Wide unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations without priority or protection.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Building stairs and parked vehicles narrow the effective walking width on the right side of the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at intersections to provide designated crossing points and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add center lines and parking lane markings to organize traffic and visually narrow the travel lanes to slow speeds.

result.summary: The environment is a narrow shared-use space lacking any formal pedestrian separation or sidewalks. Parked vehicles significantly constrain the available walking area, forcing pedestrians into the path of potential vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of separated walkway
hazards.description: Pedestrians are forced to share the narrow roadway with vehicles due to the absence of a sidewalk.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars block the path and reduce visibility for both pedestrians and drivers in a confined space.

interventions.title: Shared Street (Woonerf) Treatment
interventions.description: Redesign the space as a formal shared street with textured paving and traffic calming to prioritize pedestrians.

interventions.title: Parking Management
interventions.description: Remove or consolidate on-street parking to create a clear, unobstructed path for pedestrians.
